correctness.rationale: With selected originals A and omitted originals C, edge-nodes inside A are impossible (induced degree two), and all edge-nodes inside C must be selected since otherwise they could be added as isolated vertices. Each chosen original with a neighbor in C needs exactly one chosen crossing edge-node, by addability and the degree bound. An omitted original is blocked exactly when it has at least two selected C–C edge-nodes or has a selected crossing neighbor that would acquire a second endpoint. This is precisely the required image condition at degrees zero and one. The same obstructions prove the converse and the exponents, with empty domains and isolated originals handled. In the biclique, omission counts s,t yield independent shore maps; when a target shore is nonempty, it must be hit surjectively iff its vertices have omitted-induced degree at most one. For a=2, s=0 contributes (1+b(b−1))z^(b+2)+bz^(b+3), s=1 contributes (2+2b)z^(2b+1), and s=2 contributes [2^b−2+b(2^(b−1)−2)+sum_{t=2}^b binom(b,t)2^(b−t)]z^(2b). This proves the claimed four-term expression with addition at coincident exponents. At b≥5 all four coefficients are positive and their exponents strictly increase, giving the stated gap; summing gives 3^b+b²+1. The graph is connected and bipartite, with subdivision vertices of degree two and independent originals, so is 2-degenerate. evidence: The set of all original vertices is a maximal dissociation set but induces an empty matching, which is not maximal as an induced matching in a nonempty subdivision. Maximal independent sets exclude the permitted single edges and can have different extension obstructions.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: One cannot obtain the claimed polynomial by turning the matching size into endpoint count or by identifying independent domination with degree-one maximality. The independent crossing choices are necessary to classify the counted sets.

evidence: The complement hits every three-vertex path exactly when the set induces maximum degree at most one, and maximality becomes inclusion-minimality of the cover.
The graph S(K_(2,b)) is a multi-theta with b paths of length four, not an ordinary three-path theta except at b=3.
Duginov et al.'s publisher abstract concerns minimum/maximum-size estimates, hardness and a tree algorithm; its full results were not accessible.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A minimal 3-path vertex-cover cardinality formula would cover the same claim by reversing degrees against the graph order; a maximal induced matching is only the edge part of a dissociation set and need not be maximal as a matching.

originality.rationale: The closest same-family catalogue statements enumerate maximal induced matchings or maximal independent sets. The closest same-set catalogue statement treats deleting a matching from a biclique, not subdividing the biclique. The inspected literature and catalogue results do not supply the selected-original/crossing-edge bijection or its precise cardinality support for this family. This is a best-of-available-evidence distinction, not a publication-priority conclusion.
residual_risks: The Duginov and Orlovich full texts were not inspected; theorem-level comparison for those papers remains open. The identified Math-Net PDF was tried, not treated as read.
Equivalent work on minimal 3-path covers or subdivided multi-theta graphs may be indexed differently. Distinct same-day records were compared by content, not chronology.

value.rationale: The bijection gives an explicit structural enumeration on every one-fold subdivision and a genuine closed form on bicliques. The four degrees isolate an unbounded internal gap for connected bipartite 2-degenerate graphs, a meaningful sparsity constraint; it is not just a total-count improvement or a re-encoding of another type of maximal set.
